chunks: And Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said:

I asked him about a man who said to his female slave, 'I have freed you and I have made your manumission your dowry.' He said: 'She is freed and she has the choice; if she wishes, she may marry him, and if she wishes, she may not. If she marries him, he must give her something. And if he said, 'I have married you and I have made your dowry your manumission,' then the marriage is valid and he does not give her anything.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a man frees his slave girl and makes her freedom her dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between manumission as a condition for marriage versus manumission as the dowry itself, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the woman's agency in marital contracts. It highlights that if the choice is left to the slave-girl, she retains the right to demand additional consideration beyond her freedom, whereas an explicit declaration of manumission as *mahr* finalizes the union without further payment. This ruling underscores the legal capacity of *ummiyah* (female slaves) to enter into binding contracts and their right to financial equity in marriage.
